items.name_it: Borse di studio cantonali (non esiste una borsa federale)
items.description: Switzerland has no federal need-based student grant: grants and loans are paid by the canton where the student's (or parents') grant-relevant domicile is. EPFL states cantonal scholarships are for Swiss or foreign students whose parents live in Switzerland, so international students coming from abroad are normally not eligible.

eligibility.residence_requirement: Parents (or the student, after years of financial independence) domiciled in the canton
eligibility.income_test: Means-tested on student and family income

items.how_to_apply: Apply to the scholarship office of the canton of grant-relevant domicile.

items.name_it: Borse di eccellenza della Confederazione Svizzera
items.authority: State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI/SBFI), Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students
items.description: Research scholarships for early-career researchers from abroad who already hold a Master's degree (any discipline), plus art scholarships for an initial Master's in an artistic field (limited countries). Open to applicants from 183 countries; a Swiss academic supervisor is required for research scholarships.

other: Research track: Master's degree already completed (postgraduate research, not Bachelor/Master studies)
Art track: initial Master's in arts, only for some countries

items.how_to_apply: Through the Swiss diplomatic representation in your country; free of charge.
items.deadline: 2027-28 call opened 20 August 2026; deadlines are country-specific (published August 2026). Decisions by end of May.

items.name_it: Borse e prestiti di studio del Canton Zurigo
items.authority: Amt für Jugend und Berufsberatung, Kanton Zürich
items.description: Means-tested grants/loans for people with grant-relevant domicile in canton Zurich (normally the parents' domicile). Foreigners qualify with a C permit, a B permit held for 5 years, as recognised refugees/stateless persons, or as EU/EFTA nationals equal-treated under agreements. From 1 Jan 2027: grant up to age 27, grant with higher own contribution 28-34, interest-free loan 35-44.

eligibility.residence_requirement: Grant-relevant domicile in canton Zurich (parents' domicile, or own after 2 years of financially independent work after a first training); non-EU: C permit or B permit for 5 years

items.how_to_apply: Online via 'Stipendien Online' (new portal from 26 November 2026); amounts can be estimated with the canton's Stipendienrechner.
items.deadline: 31 July (training starting in August) / 31 January (starting in February); applications over 6 months late are not processed
items.notes: The EU/EFTA wording on the page is generic ('countries with an agreement giving equal standing'); it does not say whether a student who moved to Zurich only to study qualifies. The domicile rule usually excludes such students.

items.name_local: Bourses et prêts d'études (OCBE, canton de Vaud)
items.name_it: Borse e prestiti di studio del Canton Vaud
items.authority: Office cantonal des bourses d'études et d'apprentissage (OCBE), Vaud
items.description: Non-repayable grants (repayable only if studies are abandoned without good reason) or loans when grant criteria are not fully met. Applicant must be Swiss or hold a residence permit, and normally have parents domiciled in Vaud (other domicile routes exist, e.g. 2 years of financially independent work in Vaud after a first training).

eligibility.residence_requirement: Swiss citizen or holder of a residence permit; parents domiciled in Vaud (or other listed domicile cases)
eligibility.income_test: Student's or parents' finances insufficient; amount from a fixed-allowance budget scale

items.how_to_apply: Online application, free; renew every year.
items.deadline: For 2026-27: from 1 April 2026; send by 30 September for full-year coverage at university/EPFL

items.name_it: Borse di studio cantonali di Ginevra, Berna e Basilea Città
items.authority: Cantonal scholarship offices of Geneva, Bern and Basel-Stadt
items.description: Cantonal grant rules for Geneva, Bern and Basel-Stadt could not be read today. EPFL mentions that Geneva-resident students (or those who applied to the Geneva grant office) are referred to the Hans Wilsdorf scholarship.
items.notes: Best starting point: EDK list of cantonal grant offices https://www.edk.ch/de/themen/stipendien/stipendienstellen (returned 403 to automated fetch).

items.name_local: Subsides à l'assurance-maladie (LAMal), canton de Vaud
items.name_it: Sussidi per il premio dell'assicurazione malattia (Vaud)
items.description: Students insured under Swiss LAMal can ask the canton for a premium reduction. EPFL states Swiss students and foreign students with a C permit may apply, and EU students may be eligible depending on their financial situation.

other: Must hold Swiss basic insurance (LAMal)
Non-EU students: eligibility not stated except with a C permit

items.how_to_apply: Apply to the cantonal office via the Vaud subsidy information linked from EPFL.
items.notes: Read on the university page, not on the canton's own page (vd.ch subsidy page not reached).

items.name_local: Prämienverbilligung / subsides LAMal (Zürich, Genève, Bern, Basel-Stadt)
items.name_it: Riduzione dei premi di cassa malati (Zurigo, Ginevra, Berna, Basilea Città)
items.description: Every canton runs its own premium-reduction scheme for people with Swiss basic insurance and modest income; rules for students and foreign students in Zurich, Geneva, Bern and Basel-Stadt could not be read today.

other: Must hold Swiss basic insurance (KVG/LAMal)

items.name_it: Abbonamento generale notturno per under 25
items.description: Unlimited 2nd-class travel on the Swiss public transport network from 7pm to 5am (to 7am on weekends and public holidays) for people under 25; no Half Fare Travelcard needed. Night supplements not included.
items.how_to_apply: Buy from SBB (on the SwissPass) until the day before your 25th birthday.
items.stackable: Can be held alongside a Half Fare Travelcard (not required).

items.name_it: Metà prezzo a tariffa giovani (16-24 anni)
items.description: Reduced price of the Half Fare Travelcard for ages 16 to under 25.
items.amount: CHF 120/year (CHF 100 loyalty renewal) vs CHF 190 for adults (2026)
items.how_to_apply: Buy from SBB; loaded on the SwissPass.

items.name_local: Prise en charge de l'abonnement unireso (jeunes jusqu'à 24 ans)
items.name_it: Abbonamento unireso pagato dal Canton Ginevra per under 25 in formazione
items.description: The Canton of Geneva pays 100% of the unireso pass for young people up to 24 inclusive who are in training in Geneva (also if living outside the canton, e.g. UNIGE students), or who live in Geneva and are in training or have low income (up to CHF 50,000/year).

other: Enrolled at UNIGE, IHEID, a Haute école or other recognised Geneva training, or Geneva resident in training/low income
SwissPass card in own name required

items.amount: 100% of the unireso pass (monthly for courses of 1 month or less; annual otherwise, subject to conditions)
items.how_to_apply: Online at unireso.com/abo with proof of enrolment; decision within 10 working days.
items.notes: The pages do not mention nationality or permit requirements.

items.name_it: Abbonamento U-Abo giovani a Basilea
items.description: Youth price of the regional U-Abo for under-25s; an annual 'Jugend BS' version is cheaper for young people with tax domicile in Basel-Stadt.

other: Jugend BS: tax domicile in Basel-Stadt

items.amount: Youth U-Abo CHF 57/month or CHF 542/year (registered in TNW area); Jugend BS CHF 365/year (prices from 10.12.2023)
items.how_to_apply: Order via tnw.ch or ticket offices.
items.notes: Price table headed 'ab 10.12.2023'; page says prices subject to change.

items.name_it: Abbonamento ZVV Junior (Zurigo) per under 25
items.description: Reduced 'Junior' NetworkPass for young people up to 24.99 years; no student-specific offer.
items.amount: Zone 110 (City of Zurich): CHF 64/month vs CHF 88 adult (2nd class)
items.how_to_apply: Buy until the day before your 25th birthday (ZVV ticket shop/SwissPass).

items.name_local: Remboursement de l'impôt à la source (Vaud)
items.name_it: Rimborso dell'imposta alla fonte per studenti (Vaud)
items.description: Tax is withheld at source on B-permit students' wages; those earning no more than CHF 28,800 a year can claim a refund.

other: B permit holder working in Vaud

items.amount: Refund of tax withheld at source
items.how_to_apply: Claim from the Vaud tax administration (impôt à la source).
items.deadline: Between 1 January and 31 March of the following year
items.notes: Read on EPFL's page, which links to vd.ch (impôt à la source); not confirmed on the canton's own page.

items.name_it: Programma svizzero-europeo di mobilità (al posto di Erasmus+)
items.authority: Movetia (Swiss national agency) and Swiss higher education institutions
items.description: Switzerland is not yet in Erasmus+: exchanges with European partners run through SEMP, under which Swiss institutions send (outgoing) and receive (incoming) students. SEMP Call 2026 funds mobility from 1 June 2026 to 31 August 2027.

other: Exchange between a Swiss institution and a European partner institution

items.how_to_apply: Through the international office of your home and host institutions.
items.notes: Public Movetia pages do not state monthly grant amounts or whether incoming students receive a grant from the Swiss host; rules are in the SEMP guide (login area). Ask the host university's international office.

items.name_it: Associazione della Svizzera a Erasmus+ dal 2027 (prevista)
items.description: The Federal Council aims for Swiss association to Erasmus+ from 2027. In case of association, mobility from 1 June 2027 can be funded under the Erasmus+ Call 2027 (KA131: each institution funds its own outgoing students); mobilities ending before 1 June 2027 can only use SEMP.
items.how_to_apply: Through the home institution's international office.
items.notes: Association is described as planned/conditional on the page read; do not present it as certain.

items.name_it: Borsa di eccellenza ETH per il Master (ESOP)
items.description: Merit scholarship for excellent Master's applicants (top 10% of their Bachelor), covering living and study costs plus a tuition waiver for the regular Master's duration. About 60 awards expected for 2027/28.

other: Master's applicants only; not if already enrolled in an ETH Master's or holding a Master's degree
Very good Bachelor results (top 10%)

items.amount: CHF 12,000 per semester (CHF 13,500 from HS27) + tuition waiver
items.how_to_apply: Via the ETH Master's application (eApply) with a thesis pre-proposal and two referees.

items.name_local: ETH Stipendien (social scholarships) for international students
items.name_it: Borse sociali ETH per studenti internazionali
items.description: Need-based supplementary scholarships for Bachelor and Master students; they do not cover all costs. Bachelor students qualify after passing the first-year exams; Master's students without an ETH BSc after at least 40 ECTS in the preceding Master's year.

eligibility.income_test: Official proof of financial circumstances required
other: Bachelor: first-year exams passed in all parts
Master without ETH BSc: at least 40 ECTS completed

items.deadline: International students' window for 2026/27: 1 September - 31 October 2026

items.name_it: Aiuti finanziari dell'Università di Zurigo
items.authority: University of Zurich, Student Financial Aid Office
items.description: International Bachelor students can apply for UZH financial support once they have earned 55 ECTS; Master's students qualify only with a Swiss Bachelor's degree (those with a foreign Bachelor must self-finance, except Swiss citizens abroad).

other: Bachelor: at least 55 ECTS earned
Master: only with a Swiss Bachelor's degree

items.how_to_apply: Through the Student Financial Aid Office (studienfinanzierung.uzh.ch).

items.name_it: Borse di eccellenza EPFL per il Master
items.description: Merit fellowship for incoming Master's students (EPFL Bachelor graduates or from other universities), with guaranteed housing; renewal for the 2nd year needs 50 ECTS and a 5.0/6 average.

other: Master's applicants
Selection on academic results, research, entrepreneurship, societal commitment

items.how_to_apply: Tick the fellowship box on the Master's application (IS-Academia).
items.deadline: 15 December (external applicants, first window) / 31 January (EPFL students, consecutive Master's)

items.name_it: Borsa sociale EPFL
items.description: Need-based scholarship. International students can apply only after completing at least one year at EPFL and only after an unexpected, sudden change in their situation (full funding must be secured before arrival). Geneva residents apply to the Hans Wilsdorf scholarship instead.

other: International students: after first year at EPFL and a sudden change in circumstances
Swiss, C-permit holders and refugees: after a cantonal grant refusal or while awaiting it

items.how_to_apply: Download and submit the 2026-2027 application form.
items.deadline: For autumn 2027 support: 1 December 2026 or 15 February 2027
items.notes: If the only change is the tripled tuition fee, EPFL says to apply for a transitional allowance instead.
